ACTING TASK (each character is fully invested in a tactic; the work happens in the eyes)
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken): keep it light — tonight is supposed to be fun.
CHEN — MOTIVE: he wants one particular guest to walk into a perfect night. TACTIC: he checks every detail with his eyes, points at what's missing and pushes for more — cheerful, grinning, enjoying himself. His line is upbeat and friendly, never barked or rude. On the fangs close-up he is pleased with himself: the grin comes before the line.
DECORATOR — easy and good-natured, a workman who likes this job; he answers without stopping work.
MARK — MOTIVE: none at all; he was ready an hour ago and has been waiting. TACTIC: conserves energy, does the minimum. His line is not a joke — he genuinely has been ready this whole time. The comedy comes from the stillness of the mask, not from a performance.
JENNY — MOTIVE: tonight she must be the one everyone looks at. OBSTACLE: nothing on the rail is good enough. TACTIC: she hunts along the rail with her eyes and her fingers, judging each costume at a glance and rejecting it without even taking it down.
ENJEE (montage) — MOTIVE: she wants tonight to be the night she gets to feel like a princess. OBSTACLE: everything she owns is plain. TACTIC: in shot 3 she tries to solve it by comparing and second-guessing; in shot 4 she solves it instead with one small magic detail — the tiara, then the glove — and treasures them as if they make it real.
ENJEE (call) — GOAL: get Ryan to say yes without sounding like she needs him there. OBSTACLE: if she pushes, he will hear how much she wanted this. TACTIC: she greets him brightly and listens hard for any hesitation in his voice.
— "Hey, Ryan! You're still coming tonight, right?" — bright, warm, eyes already expecting a yes.
— (listening to his whole sentence) — the brightness drains out of her face while she keeps it still; eyes hunting for any way he might still come.
— "Oh... No, it's okay. Don't worry about it." — SHE IS ALREADY SAD WHEN SHE SAYS IT, and she does not hide it well: quiet, flat, deflated, eyes down, no forced smile. She still says it kindly, to let him off the hook.
— "Yeah... You too." — small and quiet, already somewhere else.
— (the last look in the mirror) — not crying, just sitting with it: she sees a girl in a plastic tiara with nobody coming for her.
RYAN (voice only) — MOTIVE: he feels bad and wants to get off the phone before she hears it. TACTIC: he keeps it light and practical, as if it's just logistics.
(Safety: gaze always engaged in the task — never a frozen, glassy, unfocused stare; natural blink cadence, actors blink now and then to moisturize their eyes.)

PHYSICS
The whips carry strong horizontal motion blur that resolves into sharp frames. The ghost drape sways where Chen points near it. Hangers slide and knock along the rail with real weight; fabric sways where she pushes past it; the cape lining swings and falls. The satin glove drags against her forearm as she pulls it up. The rubber mask resists for a moment at Mark's forehead, then drops over his chin and settles heavily on his shoulders, the mane flopping once and going still. The mattress gives as he swings his legs down. On the call: natural breathing, small posture shifts, the phone pressed to the far ear, the phone lowered slowly to the desk at the end.

THE SPINE OF THE SCENE
His apology and her treatment run AT THE SAME TIME. She does not stop the bud to listen, does not turn to face him and does not answer during his lines. But TWICE WHILE HE IS TALKING HER EYES COME UP AND MEET HIS — briefly, involuntarily, and each time they hold half a second longer than either of them meant before she drops back to the wound. Those two glances are the warmest thing in the scene and the whole first half turns on them.
The two threads join at the end: the last dab, the hands coming away, her eyes lifting for good, one flat sentence — and then, after a real silence, the smile, the lunch line, and his straight-faced reply.

THE TWO GLANCES — HOW THEY PLAY
They are not looks of confrontation and not checking whether he is finished. Each one is a small involuntary lift of the eyes into his, caught and held for about half a second: something soft and nervous passes between them, neither of them quite breathes through it, and then she takes her eyes back down to the graze because looking any longer would mean answering. HIS breath catches both times — a tiny hitch in the middle of his sentence, and he carries on. Nobody smiles during either of them.

Friend two mid-story with her hands, friend one answering and laughing, both animated — and Jenny between them with her books, face quiet, eyes unfocused, giving them nothing, the pencil still going in her hand. Across this shot THE FRIENDS' VOICES BEGIN TO RECEDE, as if the room were getting longer, with a low hum rising under them.
4.2–9.6 — Shot 3, close on Jenny, the tapping continuing underneath. THE REMEMBERED EXCHANGE COMES UP ALMOST AT ONCE — first the principal, a man's voice, low and close to the door; then a pause; then her mother answering him, sharper, both muffled by wood. Underneath it the friends' conversation is still audibly going on, small and far. Her head angles a few degrees toward her left, the way you turn an ear at something you are trying to hear properly; her chin lowers; she swallows once; and as her mother's answer runs she begins to squint, brows drawing together. 9.6–10.8 — Shot 4, the pencil, her mother's line finishing over it, the yellow catching the window light.
10.8–13.4 — Shot 5, her face. The remembered voices stop and she turns the exchange over: the squint deepens, the head tips a fraction the other way, her lips press together. 13.4–14.6 — Shot 6, the pencil. Two more taps; then it STOPS, dead.
14.6–20.0 — Shot 7, the medium, slowly pushing in. HER OWN VOICE GOES THROUGH HER HEAD — the question, then the second one, then the flat impossible fact — and SHE DOES NOT SPEAK. Her lips stay closed and completely still; no mouthing, no whisper, no jaw movement. Everything happens in the face around the mouth: the brows lifting slightly on the first question, the eyes going still and then searching fast on the second, the small not-quite-shake of the head on the third, the breath going out through her nose at the end. AT BOTH EDGES OF THE FRAME THE TWO FRIENDS ARE STILL TALKING TO EACH OTHER AND STILL MOVING — hands, shoulders, a laugh — and their voices are continuously audible underneath her interior voice. 20.0–22.4 — Shot 8, close, HELD. Her face after the thought, doing nothing but thinking: openly puzzled, brows still drawn, eyes moving in small increments as she keeps testing it and keeps failing. 22.4–26.4 — Shot 9, the two-shot. THE INTERRUPTION. Friend one, in the middle of saying something to friend two, breaks off mid-sentence, turns, leans across and PUTS A HAND ON JENNY'S SHOULDER — and the room's sound comes straight back to normal volume with the touch. ACTING TASK — JENNY (fully invested in her tactic; the work happens in her eyes)
SCENE DIRECTION (shared with the friends, unspoken): break time, three girls, a story.
MOTIVE (her fuel): yesterday she stood outside a door and heard the principal ask her mother how she had been, in the voice of a man who already knew her — and heard her mother shut it down with a sentence that had twenty years inside it. She has not slept.
GOAL: make that exchange fit something she already knows.
OBSTACLE: it does not fit anything, and every time she tries, the room goes further away.
TACTIC: she has stopped bothering to keep up with the conversation at all — she just sits in it and works the problem with her eyes, replaying the door, replaying both voices and the tone between them, hunting the memory for a man she might have missed. The questions never leave her mouth; it all runs inside and only the face shows the working. When the hand lands on her shoulder she is genuinely interrupted, and she does the minimum required to be left alone: the fast yes, the fast smile — and the second the friend turns away she stops paying for it and goes back down.
Moment to moment:
— the pencil at the top — she does not know she is doing it.
— the corner — nothing from her; she sits, eyes elsewhere, while the two of them talk.
— the principal's voice — the head angles toward it like an ear at a door; it is the FAMILIARITY in it she is listening to, not the words.
— her mother's answer — the squint starts; that sentence is the part that will not go anywhere.
— the eyes flicking left — toward a door that is not there.
— the pencil stopping — the thought lands.
— "Were they… acquainted before?" — thought, not said; the brows lift a fraction; the mouth does not move.
— "But how?" — thought; the eyes search fast through years; the mouth does not move.
— "I've never seen a man around my mom since I was born." — thought; the smallest not-quite-shake of the head; the breath goes out; the mouth does not move.
— the held close — still inside it; the puzzlement is not resolving.
— the hand on her shoulder — a real interruption; a beat of not having heard; then the reflex.
— "Yeah— yeah, I'm okay." — too quick, the smile switched on and off like a light; the eyes never join in.
— the tail — the mask comes off the instant she is not being looked at; the eyes go down; the same face returns; the pencil starts again. Nothing has been resolved and she is not going to stop.
(Safety: she is thinking, not vacant — gaze always engaged in the task, never a frozen glassy stare, never motionless; natural blink cadence.)

THE FRIENDS — alive, animated and unaware for the entire part: friend two tells a story with her hands from the desk in front, friend one answers, laughs and interrupts from the desk beside. They talk to each other across Jenny without pause, without going quiet and without turning to look at her — until the single moment at 22.8 when friend one breaks off mid-sentence, touches Jenny's shoulder and asks. She takes the answer at face value and turns straight back to friend two, picking the conversation up again and continuing through the whole tail. Their words stay below intelligibility apart from that one line.

Her other hand rests flat on the open notebook page; the stacked textbooks sit square in front of her. She sits with one boot hooked on the chair rung; the chiffon ruffles move slightly with her breath; her head drifts and tips in small real degrees, never snapping. The friends shift their weight on the desktops continuously, gesture and lean toward each other. Friend one's hand on Jenny's shoulder has real weight and Jenny's shoulder gives under it slightly; when it lifts away, the fabric settles. SHE SAYS NOTHING OUT LOUD UNTIL THE LAST EXCHANGE. Her question is thought, not spoken: HER LIPS DO NOT MOVE, she does not mouth it, does not whisper it, and her jaw stays closed.

GOAL: make that exchange fit something she already knows.

When the hand lands on her shoulder she does the minimum required to be left alone: the fast yes, the fast smile, and straight back into it.

— the voices sinking — she does not notice them go; the head drifts and the chin lowers.
— the touch on her arm — nothing reaches her.
— the principal's voice — the head angles toward it like an ear at a door; it is the FAMILIARITY in it she is listening to, not the words.
— her mother's answer — the squint starts; that sentence is the part that will not go anywhere.
— the eyes flicking left — toward a door that is not there.
— the pencil stopping — the thought lands.
— "Were they… acquainted before?" — thought, not said; the brows lift a fraction; the mouth does not move.
— "But how?" — thought; the eyes search fast through years; the mouth does not move.

— the held close — she is still inside it; the puzzlement is not resolving.
— the hand on her shoulder — a beat of not having heard; then the reflex.

THE EVENT OF THE SCENE — being wanted, and having it confiscated. Everything in these ten seconds is one process: a question asked in a dream and unanswered on waking. Her last

SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken, played by both): do not break the spell — behave as though all of this were completely normal.

no body in this dream and almost no words, so all of her doing is where her eyes go, how long they stay, and how much corridor she surrenders. RYAN through ADVANCING — one unbroken
approach that never pauses, never slows and never asks.
THE CONTRAST. Enju is UNCHOSEN but awake to it; Ryan is UNREAL but completely certain. The essential axis the audience reads is whether being wanted is real — she is the one who
doubts it, he is the one who never has.

ACTING TASK — ENJU (fully invested in her tactic; we are inside her, so the work is in where the looking goes and in what her feet do)
MOTIVE (her fuel): nothing this good has ever been aimed at her, and some part of her already knows it cannot be real — which is exactly why she will not look away.
GOAL: find out whether this is being aimed at her, and survive being looked at while she works it out.
OBSTACLE: he will not stop coming, and there is barely a metre and a half of corridor behind her.
TACTIC: she looks, and the looking is slow, and she barely says anything — the amazement stays inside her. She does not recognise him through the steam, so she waits rather than
searches. The moment his face resolves she stops assessing him and starts quietly failing to understand — she is asking a real question and getting no answer. Then she does the
only thing a body does when something impossible walks at it: she gives ground, without deciding to and without looking behind her. She is not fleeing and she is not frightened;
she is making room she does not have. The corridor runs out almost at once, and stopping is not a decision either — it is simply the end of the retreat. When he arrives in her
space she stays completely still, because moving might end it. Awake, she stops looking outward and starts checking her own body for proof.

THE EVENT OF THE SCENE — being wanted, and having it confiscated. Everything in these thirty seconds is one process: a question asked in a dream and unanswered on waking. Her last
movement in the segment — her own hand on her own head — is what the whole thing has been building to, and it is a question, not a memory.
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken, played by both): do not break the spell — behave as though all of this were completely normal.
THE PHYSICAL CHANNEL. The terrain is a corridor and a bed. Each of them pursues the event through his or her own visible behaviour: ENJU through LOOKING AND GIVING GROUND — she has
no body in this dream and almost no words, so all of her doing is where her eyes go, how long they stay, and how much corridor she surrenders. RYAN through ADVANCING — one unbroken
approach that never pauses, never slows and never asks.
THE CONTRAST. Enju is UNCHOSEN but awake to it; Ryan is UNREAL but completely certain. The essential axis the audience reads is whether being wanted is real — she is the one who
doubts it, he is the one who never has.

ACTING TASK — ENJU (fully invested in her tactic; we are inside her, so the work is in where the looking goes and in what her feet do)
MOTIVE (her fuel): nothing this good has ever been aimed at her, and some part of her already knows it cannot be real — which is exactly why she will not look away.
GOAL: find out whether this is being aimed at her, and survive being looked at while she works it out.
OBSTACLE: he will not stop coming, and there are only six metres of corridor behind her.
TACTIC: she looks, and the looking is slow, and she barely says anything — the amazement stays inside her. She does not recognise him through the steam, so she waits rather than
searches. The moment his face resolves she stops assessing him and starts quietly failing to understand — she is asking a real question and getting no answer. Then she does the
only thing a body does when something impossible walks at it: she gives ground, without deciding to and without looking behind her. She is not fleeing and she is not frightened;
she is making room she does not have. Each time she stops he is closer, so she recalculates and gives a bit more. When the corridor runs out she stops, and stopping is not a
decision either — it is simply the end of the retreat. When he arrives in her space she stays completely still, because moving might end it. Awake, she stops looking outward and
starts checking her own body for proof.
Moment to moment:
— the first seconds — silence and stillness; she is not searching, she is just looking at an empty corridor full of light
— the steam and the figure — pure wordless curiosity, no fear and no excitement; she watches and lets it take as long as it takes
— the face resolving — she stops being curious and starts being lost
— "Oh... Ryan?" — her one and only line, and all of her amazement is in it: astonishment and confusion arriving together, said calmly, with half a laugh she does not finish. After
it she is silent for the whole rest of the dream
— the first step back — involuntary; her body does it before she notices
— each following step — a real recalculation, and each one is a little shorter than the last
— the last step that does not happen — she runs out and stops, and there is nothing behind her
— him arriving in her space — she stays completely still: she does not back away further, does not brace and does not look away
— her head tipping back — her own small movement to keep his face in view; she is not helping anything and not resisting anything
— him leaning in — she stops breathing and stops thinking; she is not anticipating and not deciding, she is simply not moving
— the white and the alarm — no thought and no bargaining, just one caught breath as she loses it
— the jolt — the body goes before the mind; the eyes open as part of the flinch, not after it
— the seconds after — she reads the room for where she is before she reads herself for what happened
— the hand on her own head — she is not remembering, she is checking
(Safety: in the waking shot her gaze is always engaged in a real task, never a frozen glassy stare; natural uneven blink cadence, and her eyes are dry — she is startled, not upset.
She does not scream, shout or cry out. Her single internal line is never lip-synced and her mouth does not move to it.)

— the moment his face resolves in the beam — his eyes are already on her; nothing about him has to change, and that is the effect

— arriving — one continuous movement into her space, no stopping and no waiting

BACKGROUND
There is no background action and there are no other people. The corridor is empty of everyone except Ryan for the entire dream — no students, no figures, no silhouettes, no
shapes, nobody in the distance, nobody at the frame edges and nobody passing the lens at any point. The only things moving in the frame are him, the mist, the light and the water.

DREAM LOOK — SHOT 1 ONLY
The corridor is already a dream in the very first frame. Nothing "becomes" dreamlike — it starts that way and stays. This is a good dream: warm, soft, kind and magical, never
eerie and never cold.
THE DREAMY BLUR. The whole dream image is gently out of focus in a soft, pleasant, magical way — a light optical diffusion laid over everything, the way a dream remembers a place
rather than records it. Focus is shallow and soft everywhere: the corridor, the lockers, the gilded mirrors, the chandeliers and the far end all sit in creamy defocus with soft
round out-of-focus highlights, and only he resolves — from 04.8 onward his face and his eyes are the one clean, readable, properly focused thing in the frame. The edges and
corners of the picture are softer than the centre, and the softness increases with distance until the far end of the corridor is nothing but glowing white. Highlights bleed
gently into whatever surrounds them, contrast is low and creamy, and skin, water and mist all read velvety. This is real optical softness — genuine diffusion and shallow depth of
field — steady and even for all twenty-two seconds, never smear, never doubled edges, never ghosting and never digital blur.
THE MIST. Thick white mist fills the corridor from floor to ceiling, denser with distance until the far end is nothing but pale glowing white. A heavier layer lies along the floor
and rolls slowly. It never clears.
THE STEAM. The plain door releases a heavy, slow, rolling cloud of white steam that pours out at floor level, billows to head height and feeds into the mist. He walks out of that
cloud and it keeps trailing off his shoulders and his wet hair for the whole shot.
THE LIGHT IN THE AIR. Because the air is thick, every light source is visible as volume: wide soft shafts fall from the arched windows behind him and lie across the corridor in
slanted beams, and each chandelier throws a visible warm cone downward through the mist. He passes through them one after another, so light slides slowly down his face and
shoulders and off again in a long rhythm.
THE GLINTS. The air is full of drifting motes and tiny floating specks turning slowly in the beams, some rising rather than falling. The ones nearest the lens are far out of focus
and read as big soft round points of light; the ones inside the beams catch the chandeliers and bloom into small soft sparkling glints before drifting dark again. Each time he
crosses a beam the water on his skin and the drops in his hair do the same. All of it is physically suspended in the air and lit by the light already in the corridor — never drawn
on top of the picture, never symmetrical, never moving in a pattern and never trailing behind him.
THE GLOW. Strong soft bloom around every light source, the chandeliers halating into wide soft stars, the gilded mirrors and pale panelling glowing, the edges and corners of frame
diffused and milky, blacks lifted almost to grey. The image is soft overall while his face stays clearly readable from 04.8 onward and his eyes stay sharp inside the softness.
THE TIME. Motion runs at about 50% speed with smooth realistic blur, so bodies, water, hair, steam, mist and drifting glints all move heavy, late and velvety.
No graphic overlays of any kind: no drawn stars, no cartoon twinkles, no glitter texture, no hearts, no lens flare streaks and no filters laid over the frame. Everything magical
in this dream is made of mist, steam, beams, suspended glinting particles, water, bloom, soft diffusion, shallow focus and slowed time.

Instantly and completely different: clean, sharp, flat, ordinary, in focus edge to edge. Normal contrast, honest whites, no bloom, no halation, no diffusion, no soft focus, no

STRUCTURE — TWO SHOTS, TWO WORLDS
THE DREAM is ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN SHOT lasting fourteen seconds, filmed entirely as ENJU'S OWN EYES. There are no cuts inside it, because an eye does not cut.
THE WAKING is ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN SHOT lasting six seconds, filmed from across the bedroom at mattress height. Clean, sharp, flat morning light, normal speed, no glow at all. The cut between them is hard and the change in look is total.

THE CAMERA IS HER EYES — HOW TO MAKE THIS READ
This is the most important instruction in the prompt. The dream shot is not a tracking shot, not a handheld shot and not a shot of a person. It is her vision, and it must behave like a head and a pair of eyes:
— HEIGHT. Locked at 1.6 m, her standing eye level, for the whole shot. It never rises or falls except as described.
— MOTION. Not smooth and not mechanical. The frame breathes: a slow irregular sway from side to side and a very slight rise and fall in time with her breathing, plus tiny constant micro-corrections, the way a real head never holds perfectly still. No dolly track smoothness, no gimbal glide, no drone float.
— LOOKING. When the frame turns, it turns the way a head turns: a small quick movement that arrives and settles, not a slow even pan. It makes two of these — one early, glancing a few degrees off him and back, and one small settle as he arrives.
— NO BLINKS. Her eyelids never close. The image is never wiped, never darkened at the edges, never interrupted and never dipped to black at any point in the shot. The point of view is carried entirely by the way the frame moves.
— NOBODY IS HER. No part of her body, her hands, her hair, her shoulders, her nose or her reflection is ever visible. She is not present in her own dream as a figure.
— EYELINE. Chen looks INTO the lens, because the lens is her face. His eyes meet the camera and hold it.
— PROXIMITY. Blurred shoulders and backs pass very close to the lens and out again, the way people brush past your own field of view in a corridor.
— HIS HAND ENTERS FROM THE TOP. When he reaches her, his hand comes down INTO the frame from above the top edge, palm first, and settles out of sight just past that edge — because it lands on the top of her head, which is behind the lens and never seen. The frame dips two or three degrees under it and settles.
There is no cut, no dissolve, no speed change and no reframe anywhere inside the dream shot.

THE EVENT OF THE SCENE — being wanted, and having it confiscated. Everything in these twenty seconds is one process: a question asked in a dream and unanswered on waking. Her last movement in the segment — her own hand on the top of her own head, on the spot where his hand was — is what the whole thing has been building to, and it is a question, not a memory.
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken, played by both): do not break the spell — behave as though all of this were completely normal.
THE PHYSICAL CHANNEL. The terrain is a corridor and a bed. Each of them pursues the event through his or her own visible behaviour: ENJU through LOOKING — she has no body in this dream, attention is the only thing she can do, so all of her doing is where her eyes go and how long they stay. CHEN through ARRIVING — one unbroken approach, no deviation, no detour, no acknowledgement of anything else.
THE CONTRAST. Enju is UNCHOSEN but awake to it; Chen is UNREAL but completely certain. The essential axis the audience reads is whether being wanted is real — she is the one who doubts it, he is the one who never has.

ACTING TASK — ENJU (fully invested in her tactic; in the dream we are inside her, so the work is entirely in where the looking goes)
MOTIVE (her fuel): nothing this good has ever been aimed at her, and some part of her already knows it cannot be real — which is exactly why she will not look away.
GOAL: find out whether this is being aimed at her, and then keep it.
OBSTACLE: her own alarm clock, and the fact that she has no evidence she is allowed to have this.
TACTIC: she interrogates him with her attention. She cannot see his face through the steam, so she looks, gives up, looks back — the turn of the frame is a real check on whether he is coming this way at all. The instant his face resolves she stops checking him and starts checking herself, hunting behind her own shoulder in her head for whoever he must actually be walking toward, and finding nobody. She keeps measuring the distance he has left. When he stops she does not fill the silence and cannot; she waits and lets him hold her. When the alarm comes she bargains with it, and loses. Awake, she stops looking outward entirely and starts checking her own body for proof.

— the hand arriving from above — it lands and she is still catching up
— "No no no, not yet—" — arguing with an alarm clock
— the jolt — the body goes before the mind; the eyes open as part of the flinch, not after it

He does not scan the corridor, does not greet anyone, does not check whether he is watched — he found her before we could see his face, and from then on he keeps her, holding her eyes the entire ten metres and reading her the whole way in, watching what she does with being looked at. — stepping out of the doorway — no pause and no entrance; he continues into the corridor as if he had planned to
— the ten metres — he keeps her and gives up nothing; the walk itself is the whole tactic

He steps out of the door at ten metres, turns into the centre of the corridor, and walks all ten metres straight at her without deviating. He does not stop and wait — he comes right
into her space and the lean-in is part of the same continuous movement. He never touches her.
For the waking: she lies on her side across the bed with her head on the mattress facing into the room. The window with its thin curtain is to one side, the desk and wardrobe on
the wall opposite, the alarm clock on the bedside table within arm's reach.

STRUCTURE — THREE SHOTS
SHOT 1 — THE DREAM: one single unbroken 18-second HANDHELD POINT-OF-VIEW shot, filmed entirely as ENJU'S OWN EYES. No cuts inside it, because an eye does not cut. Everything echoes.
SHOT 2 — WAKING, STILL HER EYES: one 3-second point-of-view shot of her own bedroom, seen from where her head is lying on the mattress. Dry, flat and ordinary. The echo is gone.
SHOT 3 — WAKING, ORDINARY CAMERA: one 9-second shot from across the bedroom as she gets up. Dry, flat and ordinary.

THE CAMERA IS HER EYES — HOW TO MAKE THIS READ
This applies to shots 1 and 2. The camera is not a tracking rig and not a shot of a person. It is her vision, and it must behave like a head and a pair of eyes:
— HANDHELD. The frame is held the way a real body holds a head: a constant fine organic tremor, small irregular drifts, a slight rise and fall with her breathing, and tiny
micro-corrections that never repeat. It is alive and slightly unsteady the whole time. It is NOT dolly-smooth, NOT gimbal-glide and NOT drone-float — and equally it is not violent
shake, not whipping and not judder. Think of a documentary operator holding a camera on his shoulder and breathing.
— HEIGHT AND POSITION IN THE DREAM. Locked at 1.6 m, her standing eye level. THE CAMERA NEVER TRAVELS: it does not move forward, does not move backward, does not push in and does
not pull out. Its position in the corridor is fixed for all eighteen seconds, and he grows in the frame only because he is walking closer. The tremor and drift are body motion in
place, not travel.
— LOOKING. When the frame turns, it turns the way a head turns: a small quick movement that arrives and settles, not a slow even pan.
— THE IMAGE NEVER CLOSES. There are NO eyelid effects anywhere in the point-of-view shots. The frame never wipes shut, never dips to black, never darkens from the edges and never
simulates a blink at any point. The picture stays continuously open, and shot 2 does not begin with eyelids parting.
— NOBODY IS HER. In shot 1 no part of her body, her hands, her hair, her shoulders, her nose or her reflection is ever visible. She is not present in her own dream as a figure.
— EYELINE. Chen looks INTO the lens, because the lens is her face. His eyes meet the camera and hold it.
— NOTHING IS BETWEEN THEM. There is no glass, no window, no screen, no mirror and no barrier of any kind between the camera and the corridor. The lens is her bare eyes in open air.
Nothing is ever tapped, knocked or pressed against a surface, and there is no reflection on the front of the image.
— HE NEVER TOUCHES HER. No hand ever enters the frame. Nothing comes in from any edge. There is no contact of any kind anywhere in the dream — he closes the distance with his face
only, and the frame never tilts, dips, jolts or reacts to being touched, because nothing touches her.

FIRST FRAME
Occupied immediately: the school corridor already deep in dream — thick white mist filling it from floor to ceiling, chandeliers blooming into soft haloes, broad beams of light

is completely empty. Ten metres ahead in the left-hand wall a plain door is already swinging open into a heavy billow of white steam. The frame is handheld and alive from frame one.

FORMAT MODE
Three shots, 30 seconds total. Shot 1 runs 18 seconds at roughly 50% speed. Shot 2 runs 3 seconds and shot 3 runs 9 seconds, both at 100% speed. Two hard cuts, at 18.0 s and at
21.0 s. No dissolves anywhere.

Shot 2: 84° at her eye height lying down, the same human-sight field, lens locked.
Shot 3: 63° at 2.0 m, lens locked — wide enough to hold the wrecked bed and the room around her, close enough that her face is clearly readable.

THE EVENT OF THE SCENE — being wanted, and having it confiscated. Everything in these thirty seconds is one process: something is offered in a dream and taken back on waking. The
ending is not a fright — it is a small loss, and the last frame is a girl sitting in a silent room with nothing.
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken, played by both): do not break the spell — behave as though all of this were completely normal.
THE PHYSICAL CHANNEL. The terrain is a corridor and a bed. Each pursues the event through his or her own visible behaviour: ENJU through LOOKING — she has no body in the dream and
she does not move from her spot, so all of her doing is where her eyes go and how long they stay, and on waking her looking simply has nothing left to land on. CHEN through
ARRIVING — one unbroken approach, no deviation, no pause and no contact.
THE CONTRAST. Enju is UNCHOSEN but awake to it; Chen is UNREAL but completely certain. The essential axis the audience reads is whether being wanted is real — she is the one who
doubts it, he is the one who never has.

ACTING TASK — ENJU (fully invested in her tactic; in the dream the work is entirely in where the looking goes)
MOTIVE (her fuel): nothing this good has ever been aimed at her, and some part of her already knows it cannot be real — which is exactly why she will not look away.
GOAL: find out whether this is being aimed at her, and then keep it.
OBSTACLE: her own alarm clock, and the fact that she has no evidence she is allowed to have this.
TACTIC: she does almost nothing, because she cannot. She stands where she is and looks, and the looking is slow. She does not recognise him through the steam, so she waits rather
than searches. The moment his face resolves she stops thinking about him and starts quietly failing to understand: she checks the corridor behind her in her own head for who else he
could be walking toward, finds nobody, and does not resolve it. She keeps measuring the distance he has left. When he arrives she does not step back, does not brace and does not
fill the silence — she stays exactly where she is, because moving might end it. Awake, she does not look for danger; she looks for the corridor, does not find it, and stops looking.

— "Wow. He's so..." — she does not finish it and does not try to

— the room arriving — no fright and no jolt; she takes it in slowly and recognises it, and recognising it is the bad news

BACKGROUND
There is no background action and there are no other people anywhere in the segment. The corridor is empty of everyone except Chen for the entire dream — no students, no figures, no

DREAM LOOK — SHOT 1 ONLY
The corridor is already a dream in the very first frame. Nothing "becomes" dreamlike — it starts that way and stays.
THE MIST. Thick white mist fills the corridor from floor to ceiling, denser with distance until the far end is nothing but pale glowing white. A heavier layer lies along the floor
and rolls slowly. It never clears.
THE STEAM. The plain door releases a heavy, slow, rolling cloud of white steam that pours out at floor level, billows to head height and feeds into the mist. He walks out of that
cloud and it keeps trailing off his shoulders and his wet hair for the whole shot.
THE GLOW ON HIM. He is lit from behind by the arched windows, hard and bright, so a brilliant white rim of light burns along the tops of his shoulders, down the outside of his arms,
along his jaw and all through his wet hair, separating him completely from the corridor. The mist immediately around him is lit up by that same backlight, so he moves inside his own
soft halo of glowing air that travels with him. His wet skin holds a smooth sheen wherever the light rakes across it, and the beads of water on his shoulders and the drops in his
hair act like tiny lenses, flaring into small hard points of light every time he crosses a beam. The glow is strongest at his outline and thins toward the centre of him, so the
effect is a person shining at the edges rather than a person made of light. It is created entirely by real backlight, wet skin and lit mist — not by a painted-on aura, not by a
graphic overlay and not by a filter.
THE LIGHT IN THE AIR. Because the air is thick, every light source is visible as volume: wide soft shafts fall from the arched windows behind him and lie across the corridor in
slanted beams, and each chandelier throws a visible warm cone downward through the mist. He passes through them one after another, so light slides slowly down his face and
shoulders and off again in a long rhythm, and it is crossing into the first of them that reveals his face.
THE GLINTS. The air is full of drifting motes and tiny floating specks turning slowly in the beams, some rising rather than falling. The ones nearest the lens are out of focus and
read as soft round points of light; the ones inside the beams catch the chandeliers and flare into small hard sparkling glints before drifting dark again. All of it is physically

THE GLOW OF THE ROOM. Strong soft bloom around every light source, the chandeliers halating into wide soft stars, the gilded mirrors and pale panelling glowing, the edges and
corners of frame diffused and milky, blacks lifted almost to grey. The image is soft overall while his face stays clearly readable from 05.6 onward, his eyes stay sharp, and his
mouth stays clearly readable while he speaks.
THE TIME. Motion runs at about 50% speed with smooth realistic blur, so bodies, water, hair, steam, mist and drifting glints all move heavy and late.
No graphic overlays of any kind: no drawn stars, no cartoon twinkles, no glitter texture, no hearts, no lens flare streaks, no painted aura and no filters laid over the frame.
Everything magical in this dream is made of mist, steam, backlight, suspended glinting particles, water, bloom and slowed time.

SCENE CONTEXT
The opening of an episode. A girl is dreaming, and she is inside her own dream looking out of her own eyes: the boy she likes steps out of the school changing-room door into a corridor full of steam, hair still wet, and walks the length of the corridor directly at her, looking at nothing else. Her own panicking voice runs in her head. Then an alarm clock drags her out of it and she wakes with a jolt, sideways across her bed. The dream is one unbroken look through her eyes; the waking is one unbroken ordinary shot.

STRUCTURE — TWO SHOTS, TWO WORLDS
THE DREAM is ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN SHOT lasting fourteen seconds, filmed entirely as ENJU'S OWN EYES. There are no cuts inside it, because an eye does not cut.
THE WAKING is ONE SINGLE UNBROKEN SHOT lasting six seconds, filmed from across the bedroom at mattress height. Clean, sharp, flat morning light, normal speed, no glow at all. The cut between them is hard and the change in look is total.

THE CAMERA IS HER EYES — HOW TO MAKE THIS READ
This is the most important instruction in the prompt. The dream shot is not a tracking shot, not a handheld shot and not a shot of a person. It is her vision, and it must behave like a head and a pair of eyes:
— HEIGHT. Locked at 1.6 m, her standing eye level, for the whole shot. It never rises or falls except as described.
— MOTION. Not smooth and not mechanical. The frame breathes: a slow irregular sway from side to side and a very slight rise and fall in time with her breathing, plus tiny constant micro-corrections, the way a real head never holds perfectly still. No dolly track smoothness, no gimbal glide, no drone float.
— LOOKING. When the frame turns, it turns the way a head turns: a small quick movement that arrives and settles, not a slow even pan. It makes two of these — one early, glancing a few degrees off him and back, and one small settle as he arrives.
— BLINKS. Twice in the shot her eyelids close: over three or four frames the image is wiped shut from the top and bottom edges by soft dark curved shapes that meet in the middle and immediately part again. This is a physical eyelid closing over a lens, with real motion — not a fade, not a dip to black, not a cut and not a flicker.
— NOBODY IS HER. No part of her body, her hands, her hair, her shoulders, her nose or her reflection is ever visible. She is not present in her own dream as a figure.
— EYELINE. Chen looks INTO the lens, because the lens is her face. His eyes meet the camera and hold it.
— PROXIMITY. Blurred shoulders and backs pass very close to the lens and out again, the way people brush past your own field of view in a corridor.
— HIS HAND ENTERS FROM THE TOP. When he reaches her, his hand comes down INTO the frame from above the top edge, palm first, and settles out of sight just past that edge — because it lands on the top of her head, which is behind the lens and never seen. The frame dips two or three degrees under it and settles.
There is no cut, no dissolve, no speed change and no reframe anywhere inside the dream shot.

SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken, played by both): do not break the spell — behave as though all of this were completely normal.

Each of them pursues the event through his or her own visible behaviour: ENJU through LOOKING — she has no body in this dream, attention is the only thing she can do, so all of her doing is where her eyes go and how long they stay. CHEN through ARRIVING — one unbroken approach, no deviation, no detour, no acknowledgement of anything else.
THE CONTRAST. Enju is UNCHOSEN but awake to it; Chen is UNREAL but completely certain. The essential axis the audience reads is whether being wanted is real — she is the one who doubts it, he is the one who never has.

She cannot see his face through the steam, so she looks, gives up, looks back — the turn of the frame is a real check on whether he is coming this way at all. She keeps measuring the distance he has left. When he stops she does not fill the silence and cannot; she waits and lets him hold her. When the alarm comes she bargains with it, and loses. Awake, she stops looking outward entirely and starts checking her own body for proof.

Everything is white, warm, glowing and openly unreal. The dominant impression of the whole shot is WHITE — white haze, white steam, white blooming light — with the pastel walls and gold moulding only just showing through it.

completely empty. A door opens and the boy she likes comes out of it straight from the shower, in a towel, and walks the whole length of the corridor directly at her while she
stands rooted to the spot. He arrives, strokes her hair, lifts her chin and leans in — and an alarm clock takes it away one moment before anything happens. Then she is in her own
bed with the alarm screaming. The dream is one unbroken look through her eyes with everything echoing; the waking is dry, sharp and ordinary.

THE CAMERA IS HER EYES — HOW TO MAKE THIS READ
This is the most important instruction in the prompt. The dream shot is not a tracking shot, not a handheld shot and not a shot of a person. It is her vision, and it must behave
like a head and a pair of eyes:
— HEIGHT. Locked at 1.6 m, her standing eye level, for the whole shot.
— SHE STANDS STILL. The camera never travels. It does not move forward, does not move backward, does not push in, does not pull out and does not follow anyone. Its position in the
corridor is fixed for all twenty-one seconds. He grows in the frame only because he is walking closer.
— MOTION. Not smooth and not mechanical. The frame breathes: a slow irregular sway and a very slight rise and fall in time with her breathing, plus tiny constant
micro-corrections, the way a real head never holds perfectly still. No dolly smoothness, no gimbal glide, no drone float.
— LOOKING. When the frame turns, it turns the way a head turns: a small quick movement that arrives and settles, not a slow even pan. It makes two of these across the shot.
— BLINKS. Twice in the shot her eyelids close: over three or four frames the image is wiped shut from the top and bottom edges by soft dark curved shapes that meet in the middle
and immediately part again. This is a physical eyelid closing over a lens, with real motion — not a fade, not a dip to black, not a cut and not a flicker.
— NOBODY IS HER. No part of her body, her hands, her hair, her shoulders, her nose or her reflection is ever visible. She is not present in her own dream as a figure.
— EYELINE. Chen looks INTO the lens, because the lens is her face. His eyes meet the camera and hold it.
— NOTHING IS BETWEEN THEM. There is no glass, no window, no screen, no mirror and no barrier of any kind between the camera and the corridor. The lens is her bare eyes in open
air. Nothing is ever tapped, knocked or pressed against a surface, and there is no reflection on the front of the image.
— HIS HANDS ENTER THE FRAME FROM ITS EDGES, GENTLY. First his hand rises INTO the frame from above the top edge, palm down and fingers relaxed and slightly curved, settles softly
out of sight just past that edge on her hair, and strokes slowly back over the top of her head. Then it slides down and re-enters at the BOTTOM edge, and his fingers come in under
her chin and lift it. Both movements are slow, light and affectionate. Neither is a tap, a pat, a knock, a slap or an impact of any kind — nothing is struck, nothing is hit and
neither hand ever accelerates.
— THE FRAME TILTS WHEN HER HEAD IS LIFTED. As his fingers raise her chin, the whole image tilts upward five to seven degrees, smoothly and slowly, and stays there. This is not a
camera move and not a pan — it is her head being tipped back behind the lens. The frame never jolts or shakes at any point.
There is no cut, no dissolve, no speed change and no reframe anywhere inside the dream shot.

SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken, played by both): do not break the spell — behave as though all of this were completely normal.
THE PHYSICAL CHANNEL. The terrain is a corridor and a bed. Each of them pursues the event through his or her own visible behaviour: ENJU through LOOKING — she has no body in this
dream and she does not move from her spot, so all of her doing is where her eyes go and how long they stay. CHEN through ARRIVING — one unbroken approach, no deviation, no detour,
no pause and no acknowledgement of anything else.
THE CONTRAST. Enju is UNCHOSEN but awake to it; Chen is UNREAL but completely certain. The essential axis the audience reads is whether being wanted is real — she is the one who
doubts it, he is the one who never has.

GOAL: find out whether this is being aimed at her, and then keep it.

than searches. The moment his face resolves she stops thinking about him and starts quietly failing to understand: she checks the corridor behind her in her own head for who else

STYLE
Modern Korean teen drama, live-action, natural skin texture with real pores on every face. The dream is dominated by white — white mist and steam and blooming light with glinting
suspended particles — and pastel blue, blush pink, cream and gold showing through it. The waking is white walls, honey oak, dusty pink and cool daylight. Clean digital capture with
very light grain.

QUALITY
Sharp clarity where the look calls for it, stable picture, natural colours, readable faces, controlled highlights even in the heavy white mist. The slowed dream carries smooth
realistic motion blur on the walk, the water, the hair, the steam and the drifting glints and stays temporally stable across all twenty-one seconds; the return to full speed on the

micro-corrections, the way a real head never holds perfectly still. No dolly smoothness, no gimbal glide, no drone float.
— THE RETREAT. When she gives ground, the frame moves BACKWARD in discrete uneven pushes, one per step, each with a small vertical bounce as her weight lands and a tiny sideways
wobble as her balance resets. It is a person walking backwards without looking, not a camera pulling back on rails. Between steps the frame holds and breathes. The retreat is
never continuous and never even.
— LOOKING. When the frame turns, it turns the way a head turns: a small quick movement that arrives and settles, not a slow even pan.
— BLINKS. Twice in the shot her eyelids close: over three or four frames the image is wiped shut from the top and bottom edges by soft dark curved shapes that meet in the middle

— EYELINE. Chen looks INTO the lens, because the lens is her face. His eyes meet the camera and hold it.
— NOTHING IS BETWEEN THEM. There is no glass, no window, no screen, no mirror and no barrier of any kind between the camera and the corridor. The lens is her bare eyes in open

movement in the segment — her own hand on her own head — is what the whole thing has been building to, and it is a question, not a memory.
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken, played by both): do not break the spell — behave as though all of this were completely normal.

pauses, never slows and never asks.
THE CONTRAST. Enju is UNCHOSEN but awake to it; Chen is UNREAL but completely certain. The essential axis the audience reads is whether being wanted is real — she is the one who
doubts it, he is the one who never has.

OBSTACLE: he will not stop coming, and there are only six metres of corridor behind her.

closer, so she recalculates and gives a bit more. When the corridor runs out she stops, and stopping is not a decision either — it is simply the end of the retreat. Under his hand

THE CAMERA IS HER EYES — HOW TO MAKE THIS READ

— MOTION. Not smooth and not mechanical. The frame breathes: a slow irregular sway from side to side and a very slight rise and fall in time with her breathing, plus tiny
constant micro-corrections, the way a real head never holds perfectly still. No dolly track smoothness, no gimbal glide, no drone float.
— LOOKING. When the frame turns, it turns the way a head turns: a small quick movement that arrives and settles, not a slow even pan. It makes two of these across the shot.
— BLINKS. Twice in the shot her eyelids close: over three or four frames the image is wiped shut from the top and bottom edges by soft dark curved shapes that meet in the middle
and immediately part again. This is a physical eyelid closing over a lens, with real motion — not a fade, not a dip to black, not a cut and not a flicker.

— EYELINE. Chen looks INTO the lens, because the lens is her face. His eyes meet the camera and hold it.
— NOTHING IS BETWEEN THEM. There is no glass, no window, no screen, no mirror and no barrier of any kind between the camera and the corridor. The lens is her bare eyes in open
air. Nobody touches, taps or presses against a surface at any point, and there is no reflection of anything on the front of the image.

camera move and not a pan — it is her head being tipped back behind the lens. The frame never jolts, shakes or dips at any point.

unmotivated flicker in the light, no frame-skipping stutter, no identity drift. The two eyelid closures are intended and are the only interruptions of the image.

ACTING TASK — RYAN (fully invested in his tactic; the work happens in his eyes)
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken): get her to stop before the door.
MOTIVE (his fuel): if she goes through that door without hearing him, the version of him she carries in there is the liar, and that version sets.
GOAL: one sentence before the door.
OBSTACLE: the floor, and then the door.
TACTIC: from the floor he does not try to get up first — he shouts first, because the door is closer than his feet are. He watches off-frame for the turn that does not come, and when
the door slams his eyes stay on it for a full second before they drop.
Moment to moment:
— the trip — he is looking at her off-frame, not at the floor, which is why he falls.
— the landing — real winded shock, and then he immediately discards it; the pain never becomes the subject.
— "Enjee, wait…" — thrown from the floor past the lens, all breath.
— "…let me explain…" — quieter; he already knows, off-frame, that her hand is on the door.
(Safety: gaze always engaged in the task — never a frozen, glassy stare; natural blink cadence.)

ACTING TASK — ENJEE (fully invested in her tactic; the work happens in her eyes)
Corridor — SCENE DIRECTION: get through the door. MOTIVE: if she turns around she will cry in front of him. GOAL: the bathroom. TACTIC: she looks only at the door handle and lets his
voice hit her back. The refusal to turn is the whole performance and it is played entirely with her back and her shoulders.
Classroom — SCENE DIRECTION (shared with the friends, unspoken): be normal, make this an ordinary afternoon. MOTIVE (her fuel): she has had a day nobody in this room knows about, and
a joke from a friend is the first thing that has not asked anything of her. GOAL: stay in the laugh as long as it lasts. OBSTACLE: the window behind her. TACTIC: she gives the

does not decide to stop laughing; it stops because her attention has gone downstairs, and she is checking whether that is really him.
Moment to moment:
— the walk to the door — her shoulders are up and locked; she is holding something in with her whole upper body.
— the hand on the handle — no hesitation, because hesitating would be visible from behind.
— on the sill — comfortable, unguarded, sitting the way you sit with people you trust.
— the laugh — full and real, given to the friend who earned it.
— the turn over her shoulder — pulled, not chosen. The body stays where it is; only the head goes.
— looking down through the glass — reading the red jacket, then the bike, then confirming the hair; the mouth stays open from the laugh.

THE CAMERA IS HER EYES — HOW TO MAKE SHOT 1 READ
This is the most important instruction in the prompt. The dream shot is not a tracking shot, not a handheld shot and not a shot of a person. It is her vision, and it must behave

— HEIGHT. Locked at 1.6 m, her standing eye level, for the whole shot.
— MOTION WHILE STANDING. Not smooth and not mechanical. The frame breathes: a slow irregular sway and a very slight rise and fall in time with her breathing, plus tiny constant
micro-corrections, the way a real head never holds perfectly still. No dolly smoothness, no gimbal glide, no drone float.
— THE RETREAT. When she gives ground, the frame moves BACKWARD in two discrete uneven pushes, one per step, each with a small vertical bounce as her weight lands and a tiny
sideways wobble as her balance resets. It is a person walking backwards without looking, not a camera pulling back on rails. Between the steps the frame holds and breathes. The
retreat is never continuous and never even, and the second step is shorter than the first.
— LOOKING. When the frame turns, it turns the way a head turns: a small quick movement that arrives and settles, not a slow even pan.

— EYELINE. Ryan looks INTO the lens, because the lens is her face. His eyes meet the camera and hold it.
— NOTHING IS BETWEEN THEM. There is no glass, no window, no screen, no mirror and no barrier of any kind between the camera and the corridor. The lens is her bare eyes in open

diagonally across the frame with her head near the upper corner, so that when her eyes snap open she is staring straight up INTO the lens. The wrecked bedding fills the rest of
the frame around her.
Setup C — FROM THE SIDE. Camera 1.0 m high, 1.8 m out from the long side of the bed, aimed straight across it, static. Once she is sitting up this sits at about her chest height
and reads as a normal level view from across a small bedroom. It holds her sitting figure with room above her head for her raised arms and her hair, and keeps the twisted duvet
and the pillow on the floor at the edges of frame.
The two waking angles are deliberately opposite — straight down, then straight across — so the hard cut between them reads instantly.

00.0-00.7 the empty corridor, thick with mist and drifting glints of light, beams lying across the air, the whole picture softly diffused and glowing. The frame sways gently with
her breathing. Three metres ahead the door in the left-hand wall is already swinging open and a huge slow billow of white steam rolls out into the corridor and spreads.
00.7-01.6 he steps out of the doorway inside the steam and turns into the centre of the corridor, already walking toward the lens. Backlit by the far windows, he reads as a soft
dark shape in a white glow, with a rim of light along the shoulders and the wet hair. No face yet. She thinks nothing in words — she simply keeps looking, and the frame stays on

02.6-03.4 she gives ground: the frame pushes BACKWARD one step with a small bounce as her weight lands, then holds and breathes. He closes the distance again immediately, so the

06.4-07.4 she does not move again. She blinks twice, hard and fast, still staring straight up. Her eyes dart once left and once right without her head moving, reading the room for

THE EVENT OF THE SCENE — being wanted, and having it confiscated. The dream asks a question and the alarm takes the answer away one moment early, and the waking is that whole
thing detonating: she cannot sit still with it, so it comes out through her hands, her voice and a head she is trying to shake it out of. The dream is silent and slow; the waking
is loud and fast, and the distance between the two is the joke and the ache at once.
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken, played by both in the dream): do not break the spell — behave as though all of this were completely normal.
THE PHYSICAL CHANNEL. The terrain is a corridor and a bed. ENJU pursues the event through LOOKING AND GIVING GROUND in the dream — she has no body there and almost no words, so
all of her doing is where her eyes go and how much corridor she surrenders — and then, awake, through HER OWN HANDS AND HEAD. RYAN pursues it through ADVANCING — one unbroken
approach that never pauses, never slows and never asks.
THE CONTRAST. Enju is UNCHOSEN but awake to it; Ryan is UNREAL but completely certain. The essential axis the audience reads is whether being wanted is real — she is the one who
doubts it, he is the one who never has.

ACTING TASK — ENJU
MOTIVE (her fuel): nothing this good has ever been aimed at her, and some part of her already knows it cannot be real — which is exactly why she will not look away.
GOAL: in the dream, find out whether this is being aimed at her and survive being looked at while she works it out. Awake, get it out of her body before it eats her.
OBSTACLE: in the dream, he will not stop coming and there is barely a metre and a half of corridor behind her. Awake, it already happened and there is nowhere to put it.
TACTIC IN THE DREAM: she looks, and the looking is slow, and she barely says anything — the amazement stays inside her. She does not recognise him through the steam, so she waits
rather than searches. The moment his face resolves she stops assessing him and starts quietly failing to understand. Then she does the only thing a body does when something
impossible walks at it: she gives ground, without deciding to and without looking behind her. She is not fleeing and she is not frightened; she is making room she does not have.
The corridor runs out almost at once, and stopping is not a decision either. When he arrives in her space she stays completely still, because moving might end it.
TACTIC AWAKE: first pure animal fright — the body wakes before she does and she is briefly nowhere, staring up at her own ceiling with no idea where she is. Then it catches up
with her all at once: what it was, who it was, and the fact that it was hers. She cannot hold that still, so she grabs her own head and tries to physically shake it out. The
scream is not fear and not grief — it is a seventeen-year-old completely overwhelmed and mortified by her own dream, with nobody in the room to hide it from.
Moment to moment:
— the first half-second — silence and stillness; she is not searching, she is just looking at an empty corridor full of light
— the steam and the figure — pure wordless curiosity, no fear and no excitement
— the face resolving — she stops being curious and starts being lost
— "Oh... Ryan?" — her one and only line, and all of her amazement is in it: astonishment and confusion arriving together, said calmly, with half a laugh she does not finish
— the first step back — involuntary; her body does it before she notices
— the second step — a real recalculation, and shorter than the first
— the wall behind her — she runs out and stops, and there is nothing behind her
— him arriving in her space — she stays completely still: she does not back away further, does not brace and does not look away
— her head tipping back — her own small movement to keep his face in view
— him leaning in to kiss her — she stops breathing and stops thinking; she is not anticipating and not deciding, she is simply not moving
— the jolt from above — the body goes before the mind; the eyes open as part of the flinch, not after it, and they open onto nothing she recognises
— the second after — she reads the room for where she is before she reads herself for what happened
— sitting up — abrupt and uncoordinated, no grace in it at all
— the hands into her hair — this is the moment she understands what she just dreamed; the grab is fast and hard and she does not let go
— the scream and the head shake — everything at once and nothing chosen; she is trying to shake it out of her own skull
— the last held frame — she is not calmer, she has just run out of scream
(Safety: her eyes are dry throughout — she is startled and mortified, not upset and not crying. The scream is one short strangled burst, not a horror-film scream and not a
sustained shriek. Her gaze is always engaged in a real task, never a frozen glassy stare, with a natural uneven blink cadence. Her single internal line in the dream is never
lip-synced and her mouth does not move to it.)

ACTING TASK — RYAN (fully invested in his tactic; the work happens in his eyes)
MOTIVE (his fuel): in her dream he has never once doubted anything, least of all whether she wants him to walk over.
GOAL: close the distance, keep closing it, and kiss her.
OBSTACLE: none, and the total absence of hesitation is what makes him magnetic.
TACTIC: he refuses to hurry and refuses to look anywhere else. He found her before we could see his face, and from then on he keeps her, holding her eyes the whole way in and
reading her the entire time — watching what she does with being looked at and with being walked at. He does not react to her giving ground, does not acknowledge it and does not
slow for it; he simply takes back whatever she gives up. He does not stop and wait at any point, because stopping would be a question and he has none. Then he comes the last of
the way in and leans in to kiss her, and he never once reaches for her.
Moment to moment:
— stepping out of the doorway — no pause and no entrance; he continues into the corridor as if he had planned to
— the approach — he keeps her and gives up nothing; the walk itself is the whole tactic
— the moment his face resolves in the beam — his eyes are already on her; nothing about him has to change, and that is the effect
— each step she retreats — he answers it without registering it, and gains a little
— arriving — one continuous movement into her space, no stopping and no waiting
— "Hey." — low and easy, thrown into the middle of his own movement, and he watches it land
— deciding to kiss her — no decision is visible, because he made it before the shot started; the lean is simply the next thing his body does
— leaning in — the same tempo as everything else; his hands stay exactly where they are, he never reaches out and never touches her, he is not rushing to it and he never gets there
(Safety: eyes wide open with the full iris and a bright catchlight visible, never half-shut, drooping or squinting; steady unbroken eye contact with the lens from the moment his
face is readable; natural blink cadence. He never looks down at his own body, never adjusts the towel for effect and never breaks his own rhythm.)

BACKGROUND
There is no background action and there are no other people. The corridor is empty of everyone except Ryan for the entire dream — no students, no figures, no silhouettes, no
shapes, nobody in the distance, nobody at the frame edges and nobody passing the lens at any point. The only things moving in the frame are him, the mist, the light and the water.
The bedroom contains nobody but Enju.

DREAM LOOK — SHOT 1 ONLY
The corridor is already a dream in the very first frame. Nothing "becomes" dreamlike — it starts that way and stays. This is a good dream: warm, soft, kind and magical, never
eerie and never cold.
THE DREAMY BLUR. The whole dream image is gently out of focus in a soft, pleasant, magical way — a light optical diffusion laid over everything, the way a dream remembers a place
rather than records it. Focus is shallow and soft everywhere: the corridor, the lockers, the gilded mirrors, the chandeliers and the far end all sit in creamy defocus with soft
round out-of-focus highlights, and only he resolves — from 01.6 onward his face and his eyes are the one clean, readable, properly focused thing in the frame. The edges and
corners of the picture are softer than the centre, and the softness increases with distance until the far end of the corridor is nothing but glowing white. Highlights bleed
gently into whatever surrounds them, contrast is low and creamy, and skin, water and mist all read velvety. This is real optical softness — genuine diffusion and shallow depth of
field — steady and even for all six seconds, never smear, never doubled edges, never ghosting and never digital blur.
THE MIST. Thick white mist fills the corridor from floor to ceiling, denser with distance until the far end is nothing but pale glowing white. A heavier layer lies along the floor
and rolls slowly. It never clears.
THE STEAM. The plain door releases a heavy, slow, rolling cloud of white steam that pours out at floor level, billows to head height and feeds into the mist. He walks out of that
cloud and it keeps trailing off his shoulders and his wet hair for the whole shot.
THE LIGHT IN THE AIR. Because the air is thick, every light source is visible as volume: wide soft shafts fall from the arched windows behind him and lie across the corridor in
slanted beams, and each chandelier throws a visible warm cone downward through the mist. He passes through them one after another, so light slides slowly down his face and
shoulders and off again.
THE GLINTS. The air is full of drifting motes and tiny floating specks turning slowly in the beams, some rising rather than falling. The ones nearest the lens are far out of focus
and read as big soft round points of light; the ones inside the beams catch the chandeliers and bloom into small soft sparkling glints before drifting dark again. Each time he
crosses a beam the water on his skin and the drops in his hair do the same. All of it is physically suspended in the air and lit by the light already in the corridor — never drawn
on top of the picture, never symmetrical, never moving in a pattern and never trailing behind him.
THE GLOW. Strong soft bloom around every light source, the chandeliers halating into wide soft stars, the gilded mirrors and pale panelling glowing, the edges and corners of frame
diffused and milky, blacks lifted almost to grey. The image is soft overall while his face stays clearly readable from 01.6 onward and his eyes stay sharp inside the softness.
THE TIME. Motion runs at about 70% speed with smooth realistic blur, so bodies, water, hair, steam, mist and drifting glints all move heavy, late and velvety while he still covers
the whole distance inside the six seconds.
No graphic overlays of any kind: no drawn stars, no cartoon twinkles, no glitter texture, no hearts, no lens flare streaks and no filters laid over the frame. Everything magical
in this dream is made of mist, steam, beams, suspended glinting particles, water, bloom, soft diffusion, shallow focus and slowed time.
WAKING LOOK — SHOTS 2 AND 3 ONLY
Instantly and completely different: clean, sharp, flat, ordinary, in focus edge to edge. Normal contrast, honest whites, no bloom, no halation, no diffusion, no soft focus, no
mist, no steam, no particles, no glow of any kind, full 100% speed. It should feel like the picture has been slapped awake at the same moment she has, and both waking shots match
each other exactly in grade, sharpness and light.

PHYSICS
HIS POSTURE THROUGHOUT THE DREAM: spine tall, chin level, shoulders open and back, free arm loose at his side, weight rolling smoothly from foot to foot in a long even unhurried
stride. None of it changes at any point.
The steam rolls out of the doorway with real volume and weight, spreads along the floor and rises, and thins as it travels. Water beads and runs slowly on his shoulders and drips
from the ends of his wet hair; each drop falls late and heavy. The towel hangs with real terry-cloth weight and swings a beat behind his stride, and the low mist swirls and parts
around his legs as he moves through it and closes again behind him. His wet strands stay stuck to his forehead. At the end he leans in from the hips and the spine with real weight
and no acceleration, his hands staying exactly where they are, and the frame tilts up slowly and settles rather than being knocked.
Her retreat has real body mechanics even though she is unseen: each backward step lands slightly heavily because she is not looking where she is going, giving the frame a small
vertical settle and a tiny sideways balance correction, and the pause between the two steps is uneven.
Awake, the bedding has real cloth behaviour: the duvet is genuinely twisted and heavy where it has been kicked, the sheet is rucked into folds under her, the throw lies crumpled on
the floor where it fell and the pillow is on its side on the floor. Her hair is authentically slept-in — flattened on one side, knotted and static-lifted on the other, some of it
stuck to her cheek. Her pyjamas are rucked and creased from a night of sleeping in them. The jolt is a real whole-body flinch that moves the mattress and the bedding with it, and
when she bolts upright the mattress compresses and rebounds. When she grabs her hair, real handfuls of it gather and pull tight in her fists and the scalp tugs visibly; when she
shakes her head the loose hair swings out and settles late, a beat behind the head, and the sleep mask slides and flops on her forehead without coming off. Her whole upper body
rocks slightly with the shake and the mattress moves under her.

LIGHTING
DREAM: warm concealed ceiling light and glowing chandeliers along the corridor, bright bloom off the mirrors and the pale panelling, and strong soft daylight from the arched
windows at the far end directly behind him, giving him a warm rim and creating the beams he walks through. Everything reads bright and washed toward white. His face stays clearly
readable once he is in the light and is the one clean point inside the soft image, with a bright catchlight in each eye.
WAKING: flat, plain early morning daylight through the thin white curtain from one side, cool and honest, filling the small room evenly and identically in both waking shots. The
bedside lamp is still on and reads as a weak warm point the daylight has beaten. From directly above, the light falls across her face without hard shadows and her eyes stay
readable. No styling, no glow, no beauty smoothing, real skin texture with visible pores.

AUDIO
The soundtrack consists of Enju's one internal line, Ryan's one line, and the honest sounds of the two places, including the sounds she actually makes on waking. Nothing else.
EVERYTHING IN THE DREAM ECHOES. For the whole of shot 1 every sound sits inside a long, soft, cavernous reverb, as if the corridor were far bigger than it looks — voices arrive
doubled and trailing, consonants smear, tails hang on and decay slowly, and everything sounds slightly distant and slightly underwater even when it is close. This applies to her
voice, his voice and every ambient sound without exception.
ENJU'S INTERNAL VOICE — FIXED CHARACTERISTICS. She has exactly one internal line in the whole segment. A seventeen-year-old girl's voice: light and youthful, fairly high in pitch,
thin and breathy rather than full, soft and unpolished — not a trained or actorly voice. Natural conversational English with a light Korean accent. She speaks SLOWLY and QUIETLY,
with air around the words, half-finishing the sentence and trailing off. This is wonder and confusion, not panic — she is not shrieking, not squealing and not excited; she sounds
like someone quietly amazed and completely unable to explain what she is looking at. Barely above a whisper, close and intimate, as if thought rather than performed, and wrapped
in the same long dream reverb. Never announced, never narrated, never the voice of an adult woman, and never spoken aloud.
RYAN'S LINE. His single spoken word is warm, low, relaxed and unhurried, close to the lens and carrying the same long reverb.
THE DREAM PLACE. Almost nothing, because the corridor is empty: the soft hiss and roll of steam, water dripping slowly, and his unhurried footfalls arriving out of the white —
all of it echoing down a corridor that sounds far too large.
THE HARD CUT. At 06.0 s the echo stops dead. The reverb does not fade — it is gone in one frame, replaced by the dry, close, boxy acoustic of a small bedroom. That switch from
enormous echo to no echo at all is the sound of waking up. The acoustic does not change again across the second waking cut.
THE ALARM AND THE ROOM. A cheap repeating electronic alarm clock beep. It cuts in faint and wrong underneath the last beat of the dream at about 05.4 s, grows through the lean-in,
and on the hard cut becomes loud, close, dry and in the room. It continues at that level to the last frame and is never switched off. With it, the honest close sound of a small
bedroom: bedding shifting, a mattress creaking, her breathing, a distant street outside the window.
THE WAKING SOUNDS. On the jolt at 06.0 there is one sharp involuntary intake of breath through the mouth — short and unvoiced — and then fast audible breathing. At 08.5 she lets
out ONE short strangled scream: a mortified, muffled, half-swallowed shriek that lasts well under a second and then breaks off into breath. It is not a horror scream, not a
sustained shriek and not words. After it, only hard breathing under the alarm to the final frame. Every one of these sounds is dry and close, with no reverb at all.

STYLE
Modern Korean teen drama, live-action, natural skin texture with real pores on every face. The dream is a good dream — warm, soft, blurred, glowing and magical — dominated by
white: white mist and steam and blooming diffused light with glinting suspended particles, and pastel blue, blush pink, cream and gold showing softly through it. The waking is
white walls, honey oak, dusty pink and cool daylight. Clean digital capture with very light grain.

QUALITY
The dream is intentionally soft, and that softness is a controlled optical look — genuine diffusion and shallow depth of field, even and stable across all six seconds — never
digital smear, never ghosting, never doubled edges and never a compression mush. Inside that softness his face and eyes stay clean and readable from 01.6 onward. Both waking shots
are sharp edge to edge and match each other exactly. Stable picture, natural colours, controlled highlights even in the heavy white mist and bloom. The slowed dream carries smooth
realistic motion blur on the walk, the water, the hair, the steam and the drifting glints and stays temporally stable throughout; the return to full speed and full sharpness on the
hard cut is a clean instant change with no ramp artefacts. The breathing sway and the two backward retreating steps of the point-of-view shot are organic and never become shake,
judder or wobble. Natural 180-degree shutter cadence in the waking shots: the jolt, the fast head shake and the flying hair carry brief directional motion blur and then resolve
into readable holds, with her face readable at every hold. Identity is locked across both waking shots — the same face, hair and pyjamas from the overhead angle and from the side.
Hands keep correct human anatomy with five fingers, including both hands gripping her hair and the hand holding the towel closed. No duplicated limbs, no extra fingers, no
ghosting, no strobing or unmotivated flicker in the light, no frame-skipping stutter, no identity drift. The dream image runs completely unbroken from the first frame to the hard
cut, with no eyelid closures and no interruptions of any kind.

SCENE CONTEXT
The opening of an episode. A girl is dreaming, and she is inside the dream looking out of her own eyes. The corridor of her school is full of mist and floating light. A door opens
and the boy she likes comes out of it straight from the shower, in a towel, and walks at her — and then keeps coming, closer and closer, while she backs away step by step until
she has nowhere left to go. He leans in, and an alarm clock takes it away one moment before anything happens. Then she is in her own bed with the alarm screaming. The dream is one
unbroken look through her eyes — soft, blurred, glowing and magical, with everything echoing; the waking is dry, sharp and ordinary.
